title: What the Traveller Keeps Out of a Third Party's Compensation
content:
Where a deductible was withheld from the settlement a third party's compensation answers on a policy of the
Travel Protection Plans, that much of the compensation is the traveller's own and is set aside before the
insurer's share is worked out. Both the deductible withheld and the settlement it was taken from stand on the
policy's own claim record.

## The three readings

1. Where a deductible was withheld from the settlement the compensation answers and the compensation counted is
   more than that deductible, what is set aside for the traveller is the deductible withheld from that
   settlement.
2. Where a deductible was withheld from that settlement and the compensation counted is no more than that
   deductible, what is set aside for the traveller is the whole of the compensation counted.
3. In every other case nothing is set aside for the traveller.

The boundary between the first two readings is the point at which the compensation counted equals the deductible
withheld. At that point the second reading governs, because it is the one that holds where the compensation is
no more than the deductible, and the whole of the compensation counted is set aside.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A deductible of 100.00 was withheld from the settlement. Where the compensation counted is 450.00, the first
reading holds and 100.00 is set aside. Where it is 100.00 exactly, the second reading holds and the whole 100.00
is set aside. Where it is 60.00, the second reading holds again and the whole 60.00 is set aside. Where no
deductible at all was withheld from that settlement, nothing is set aside, whatever the compensation counted
comes to.
